paragraphs.text: Both of you are now retired. You confirmed that your objectives and circumstances remain unchanged since the last review, and both of you continue to be comfortable with the balanced approach to risk we agreed.
At present, neither of you require any income from your investment portfolio.
You mentioned planning a holiday for the autumn; while this does not affect the advice, you were keen to raise it.
Your agreed risk profile is 5 – balanced.
We discussed investing the full value of your joint General Investment Account.
The recommended source of funds for this is your joint General Investment Account.
The recommendation is to top up both David's and Susan's Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year.
This recommendation involves the sale of existing investments.
We agreed to disinvest the joint GIA in full and to split the proceeds equally to top up both David's and Susan's Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year.
We agreed to disinvest the joint GIA in full and use the proceeds to top up both David's and Susan's Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year, split equally between the two ISAs.

It was also recorded that the investment amount is the full value of the joint GIA, with the funds coming from the joint General Investment Account and directed into top ups of both Stocks & Shares ISAs, and that this involves selling existing investments.
Selling down the General Investment Account constitutes a disposal and may result in a capital gains position to consider, which will be assessed against the annual exempt amount.
